chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt, borrows money, and performs Hajj. He said, 'If he has capacity in his wealth, there is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform Hajj if one has an outstanding debt?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that carrying debt does not inherently prohibit Hajj, provided the individual possesses sufficient assets ('wajh fi mal') to settle it or has the means to do so. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that Hajj is obligatory only after fulfilling financial obligations, distinguishing between insolvency and temporary liquidity constraints.
